en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on False Speech, 5.
The Training Rule on Sleeping Together.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Āḷavī at the Aggāḷava Shrine.
Now at that time, lay followers came to the monastery to hear the Dhamma.
When the Dhamma had been spoken, the elder bhikkhus went to their respective dwellings.
But the junior bhikkhus remained right there in the assembly hall with the lay followers, lying down heedless, lacking clear comprehension, naked, groaning, and snoring.
The lay followers were indignant, critical, and complained, saying, "How can these venerable ones,
being unmindful and lacking clear comprehension, lie down naked, moaning and snoring?
The monks heard those lay followers who were indignant, critical, and complaining.
Those monks who were few in desires... [as before] ...were indignant, disparaged, and complained, saying:
"How can these monks share a sleeping place with one who is not fully ordained?
Then those monks, having rebuked those junior monks in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the monks are sharing a sleeping place with one who is not fully ordained?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can those foolish men share a sleeping place with one who is not fully ordained?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule: ‘If a monk should share a sleeping place with one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.’"
“Whosoever bhikkhu should share a sleeping place with one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.
Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Āḷavī for as long as he pleased, set out on a wandering tour toward Kosambī.
Wandering on his tour by stages, he arrived at Kosambī. There, the Blessed One stayed at Kosambī in the Badarika Monastery.
The monks said this to the Venerable Rāhula:
“Friend Rāhula, a training rule has been laid down by the Blessed One: ‘One should not share a sleeping place with one who is not fully ordained.’”
“Go and find a bed, friend Rāhula.
Then the Venerable Rāhula, not finding a bed, made his bed in the restroom.
Then the Blessed One, rising in the early morning at the time of dawn, went to the restroom; having arrived, he cleared his throat.
The Venerable Rāhula also coughed. “Who is there?
“It is I, Blessed One; it is Rāhula.”
“Rāhula, why are you sitting here?
Then the Venerable Rāhula reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma with reference to this cause and this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, monks, to share a sleeping place for two or three nights with one who is not fully ordained.
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:
‘If any monk should share a sleeping place for more than two or three nights with one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense entailing expiation.’”
"But whoever" means whoever of such a kind...
"monks" [is the term].
...pe... this is the meaning intended here by the term "bhikkhu.
One who is not fully ordained (*anupasampanna*) refers to everyone except a bhikkhu; the remainder is called "not fully ordained."
"More than two or three nights" means exceeding two or three nights.
"Together with" (saha).
On one side.
What is called "a bed" (seyyā) is entirely covered, entirely enclosed, mostly covered, or mostly enclosed.
"He might lie down" means:
on the fourth day, when the sun has set, if a monk lies down while one who is not fully ordained is already lying down, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If a monk is already lying down and one who is not fully ordained lies down, there is an offense of expiation.
If both lie down, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If they get up and lie down again and again, there is an offense of expiation.
If one lies down together with one who is not fully ordained, perceiving them as not fully ordained, for more than two or three nights, there is an offense of expiation.

If one stays in the same sleeping place for more than two or three nights with one who is not fully ordained, while being in doubt as to whether they are not fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one stays in the same sleeping place for more than two or three nights with one who is not fully ordained, perceiving them to be fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
If the place is half-covered and half-enclosed, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one perceives someone who is fully ordained as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one is doubtful regarding someone who is fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one perceives someone who is fully ordained as fully ordained, there is no offense.
There is no offense if she stays for two or three nights,
or if she stays for less than two or three nights.
Having stayed for two nights, if on the third night one departs before dawn and stays again—
whether it be entirely covered and entirely uncovered,
or entirely covered and entirely open— [one commits an offense].
If a monk sits while one who is not fully ordained lies down on what is mostly uncovered and mostly unenclosed, it is an offense of wrong-doing.
When a bhikkhu is lying down, one who is not fully ordained sits;
or both sit; or it is one who is insane.
"For the first offender":
thus ends the fifth training rule concerning sleeping in the same bed.
